index.html
---
name: number-presentation-rule
description: Calculator display rule - round to 10 sig digits at render time only; stored value and data-value never rounded
metadata:
  type: project
---

Decided 2026-09-12, holds for the whole calculator project:
- Displayed number: at most 10 significant digits, trailing zeros and trailing "." dropped, no thousands separators.
- Exponential only when rounded magnitude >= 1e10 or < 1e-9.
- Rounding happens only in rendering. Stored/computed value is never rounded; `data-value` on `calc-display` carries the exact value.
- While typing, the display shows the entry exactly as typed.

**Why:** rounding stored values compounds through chains (`2 ÷ 3 × 3 =` must be exactly `2`).
**How to apply:** any new feature that shows numbers goes through the render-time formatter; never round in state or compute paths.

content.text:
I couldn't reproduce this, so I didn't change any code.

**What I tested:** I ran the current `index.html` (commit c7b58f5) in headless Chromium, using both the keyboard and button clicks.

| Input | Display | Tape line |
|---|---|---|
| 0.1 + 0.2 = | 0.3 | 0.1 + 0.2 → 0.3 |
| 1 ÷ 3 = | 0.3333333333 | 1 ÷ 3 → 0.3333333333 |
| 0.1 + 0.2 = + 1 = | 1.3 | 0.3 + 1 → 1.3 |
| (0.1 + 0.2) × 3 = | 0.9 | (0.1 + 0.2) × 3 → 0.9 |
| 1 ÷ 3 × 3 = | 1 | 1 ÷ 3 × 3 → 1 |

The tape rounds numbers the same way the display does (`index.html:199` and `index.html:168`). This has been true since the tape was added.

**Where 0.30000000000000004 does appear:** in the hidden `data-value` attribute, which you only see in the page source or browser dev tools. The display has the same attribute with the same value, so the two places still agree. This is on purpose: the project rule keeps the exact value there and rounds only the text on screen. Rounding it would break things like `2 ÷ 3 × 3 =`, which must come out exactly 2.

**Likely causes:**
- The user has an old or cached copy of the page.
- They were looking at `data-value` in dev tools or a test, not the text on screen.

**What would help:** a screenshot, which page or build they used, and the exact keys they pressed. If they did mean the hidden attribute, tell me and I'll explain the trade-off before changing it.
